# zcopy

> Copy a complex double-precision vector.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import zcopy from '@rreusser/blahpack/blas/base/zcopy';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
zcopy( N, x, strideX, y, strideY ) → Complex128Array
```

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | number of complex elements |
| `x` | `Complex128Array` | in | `N` |  | input array |
| ↳ `strideX` | `integer` | in |  |  | `zx` stride length |
| `y` | `Complex128Array` | out | `N` |  | input array |
| ↳ `strideY` | `integer` | in |  |  | `zy` stride length |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `N`: number of elements in input vector(s)

</details>

**Returns** `Complex128Array`: output array

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
zcopy.ndarray( N, x, strideX, offsetX, y, strideY, offsetY ) → Complex128Array
```

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | number of complex elements |
| `x` | `Complex128Array` | in | `N` |  | source complex vector |
| ↳ `strideX` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for `zx` (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetX` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for `zx` (in complex elements) |
| `y` | `Complex128Array` | out | `N` |  | destination complex vector |
| ↳ `strideY` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for `zy` (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetY` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for `zy` (in complex elements) |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `N`: number of elements in input vector(s)

</details>

**Returns** `Complex128Array`: `zy`

**Throws**

- `RangeError` first argument must be a nonnegative integer

</section>

<!-- /.usage -->

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   `zcopy()` corresponds to the reference BLAS routine [`ZCOPY`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/BLAS/SRC/zcopy.f).

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Complex128Array from '@stdlib/array/complex128/lib/index.js';
import reinterpret from '@stdlib/strided/base/reinterpret-complex128/lib/index.js';
import zcopy from '@rreusser/blahpack/blas/base/zcopy';

// Copy complex vector zx into zy:
const zx = new Complex128Array( [ 1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0 ] );
const zy = new Complex128Array( 2 );

// Using the standard interface:
zcopy( 2, zx, 1, zy, 1 );
console.log( reinterpret( zy, 0 ) ); // eslint-disable-line no-console

// Using the ndarray interface:
zcopy.ndarray( 2, zx, 1, 0, zy, 1, 0 );
console.log( reinterpret( zy, 0 ) ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference BLAS 3.12.0 source of `ZCOPY`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

ZCOPY copies a vector, x, to a vector, y.

### Further Details

jack dongarra, linpack, 4/11/78. modified 12/3/93, array(1) declarations changed to array(\*)

</section>
